{{Short description|Theorem in geometry}}
In [[algebraic geometry]], there are various generalizations of the [[Riemann–Roch theorem]]; among the most famous is the [[Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch theorem]], which is further generalized by the formulation due to [[William Fulton (mathematician)|Fulton]] et al.

== Formulation due to Baum, Fulton and MacPherson ==
Let <math>G_*</math> and <math>A_*</math> be [[functor]]s on the [[category (mathematics)|category]] ''C'' of [[scheme (mathematics)|schemes]] [[separated scheme|separated]] and [[locally of finite type]] over the base field ''k'' with [[proper morphism]]s such that
*<math>G_*(X)</math> is the [[Grothendieck group]] of [[coherent sheaf|coherent sheaves]] on ''X'',
*<math>A_*(X)</math> is the rational [[Chow group]] of&nbsp;''X'',
*for each proper morphism ''f'', <math>G_*(f), A_*(f)</math> are the [[Direct image sheaf|direct images]] (or push-forwards) along ''f''.

Also, if <math>f: X \to Y</math> is a (global) [[local complete intersection morphism]]; i.e., it factors as a closed regular embedding <math>X \hookrightarrow P</math> into a [[smooth scheme]] ''P'' followed by a [[smooth morphism]] <math>P \to Y</math>, then let
:<math>T_f = [T_{P/Y}|_X] - [N_{X/P}]</math>
be the class in the Grothendieck group of vector bundles on ''X''; it is independent of the factorization and is called the [[virtual tangent bundle]] of&nbsp;''f''.

Then the Riemann–Roch theorem then amounts to the construction of a unique [[natural transformation]]:<ref>{{harvnb|Fulton|1998|loc=Theorem 18.3.}}</ref>
:<math>\tau: G_* \to A_*</math>
between the two functors such that for each scheme ''X'' in ''C'', the [[homomorphism]] <math>\tau_X : G(X) \to A(X)</math> satisfies: for a local complete intersection morphism <math>f: X \to Y</math>, when there are closed embeddings <math>X \subset M, Y \subset P</math> into smooth schemes,
:<math>\tau_X f^* = \operatorname{td}(T_f) \cdot f^* \tau_Y</math>
where <math>\operatorname{td}</math> refers to the [[Todd class]].

Moreover, it has the properties:
*<math>\tau_X(\beta \otimes \alpha) = \operatorname{ch}(\beta) \tau(\alpha)</math> for each <math>\alpha \in G_*(X)</math> and the [[Chern class]] <math>\operatorname{ch}(\beta)</math> (or the action of it) of the <math>\beta</math> in the Grothendieck group of vector bundles on ''X''.
*it ''X'' is a closed [[subscheme]] of a smooth scheme ''M'', then the theorem is (roughly) the restriction of the theorem in the smooth case and can be written down in terms of a [[localized Chern class]].

== The equivariant Riemann–Roch theorem ==
{{expand section|date=November 2019}}

Over the complex numbers, the theorem is (or can be interpreted as) a special case of the [[equivariant index theorem]].

== The Riemann–Roch theorem for Deligne–Mumford stacks ==
Aside from [[algebraic space]]s, no straightforward generalization is possible for [[stack (mathematics)|stacks]]. The complication already appears in the [[orbifold]] case ([[Kawasaki's Riemann–Roch]]).

The equivariant Riemann–Roch theorem for finite groups is equivalent in many situations to the Riemann–Roch theorem for [[quotient stack]]s by finite groups.

One of the significant applications of the theorem is that it allows one to define a [[virtual fundamental class]] in terms of the ''K''-theoretic virtual fundamental class.<!-- More precisely,-->
